the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning

Scanning the target column, there is a striking bimodal structure:

- **Through-hardening/tempering group** (CT≈30, DT≈30 — i.e., no separate carburizing/diffusion step): targets cluster mostly in the 200–500 MPa range, topping out at **718 MPa** for a high-C (0.62), high-RedRatio (796), Cr-bearing (0.75) tempered steel (NT=845, THT=845, THt=30, THQCr=8, TT=490, Tt=60, TCr=24).

- **Case-carburized group** (NT=930, CT=930, DT≈850–896, Dt=15–70) all show much higher fatigue strength, starting at **900 MPa** and going up to 1190 MPa, with lower carbon (~0.17–0.23), higher Cr (0.45–1.17), and process times/temperatures (Ct, DT, Dt, TT, Tt) set to specific intermediate levels.

There is a clear **gap in the data between 718 MPa and 900 MPa** — no observed sample lands near 800. Since no single training row is close to 800, the best data-driven strategy is to **linearly interpolate** between the two nearest bracketing samples (718 MPa and 900 MPa) across all variables, using a weight that lands at 800:

t = (800−718)/(900−718) ≈ 0.45

Applying this interpolation to every feature (process temps/times, chemistry, RedRatio, dA/dB/dC) produces a composite recipe that blends the "heavy tempering/high-carbon" regime with the "carburizing/case-hardening" regime — consistent with how the fatigue strength transitions between these two process families in the dataset. All interpolated values fall comfortably within the allowed ranges.
